paper.title_en: Validation of Siemens’ ρ2/3 symmetry energy scaling in sub-saturation densities
paper.abstract_en: We present a novel approach to determine the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy, Esym(ρ), at sub-saturation densities through the isoscaling phenomenon in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions. While isoscaling has traditionally been used to extract the symmetry energy coefficient at a single freeze-out density, this work demonstrates its capability to map the functional form of Esym(ρ) across a broad dynamical range. Using Classical Molecular Dynamics simulations of <math altimg="si26.svg"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mn>40</mn></msup><mtext>Ca</mtext><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><msup><mrow/><mn>40</mn></msup><mtext>Ca</mtext></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si27.svg"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mn>48</mn></msup><mtext>Ca</mtext><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><msup><mrow/><mn>48</mn></msup><mtext>Ca</mtext></mrow></math> reactions, we correlate asymptotic isoscaling parameters with the thermodynamic conditions of the participant zone post-maximum compression. Our analysis reveals an adherence to the Siemens scaling law, Esym∝ρ<sup loc="post">2/3</sup>, validating the 1970s hypothesis in the non-equilibrium environment of a nuclear reaction. A global fit across freeze-out states yields a slope of m ≈ 106 MeV fm<sup loc="post">2</sup>, aligning with the theoretical prediction for a non-interacting Fermi gas (m ≈ 108 MeV fm<sup loc="post">2</sup>). To substantiate this finding without relying on multi-parameter phase-space optimizations, we introduce an alternative validation using the heavier <math altimg="si8.svg"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mn>58</mn></msup><mtext>Ni</mtext><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><msup><mrow/><mn>58</mn></msup><mtext>Ni</mtext></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si28.svg"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mn>64</mn></msup><mtext>Ni</mtext><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><msup><mrow/><mn>64</mn></msup><mtext>Ni</mtext></mrow></math> systems. By tracking the thermodynamic expansion trajectories of the participant core throughout the sub-saturation window (0.25 ≤ ρ/ρ0 ≤ 0.80), we demonstrate that the dynamic symmetry energy trajectories collapse universally onto Siemens’ canonical (ρ/ρref)<sup loc="post">2/3</sup> scaling curve when normalized at a reference density, exhibiting an average power-law exponent of <math altimg="si29.svg"><mrow><mo>〈</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>〉</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0.61</mn></mrow></math> across the multifragmentation regime (35–65 MeV/A). Finally, extending both reaction systems to 85 MeV/A naturally delineates the domain of validity of the method, showing that the scaling behavior dissolves as the system undergoes complete nuclear vaporization. These complementary analyses establish isoscaling as a robust probe capable of mapping the density dependence of the nuclear equation of state.
